name: JPMorgan Chase

summary.text: JPMorgan Chase & Co. is a major U.S. bank. In January 2014 it entered a deferred prosecution agreement over two Bank Secrecy Act violations tied to its long banking relationship with Bernard Madoff, whose Ponzi scheme was exposed in 2008, and forfeited $1.7 billion. JPMorgan was Jeffrey Epstein's bank from 1998 until 2013, about five years past his 2008 conviction. In 2023 it agreed to pay $290 million to settle a lawsuit by Epstein's victims and $75 million to settle a suit by the U.S. Virgin Islands, without admitting liability.

facts.claim: In January 2014, JPMorgan Chase entered a two-year deferred prosecution agreement resolving two Bank Secrecy Act felony charges, including failure to file a suspicious activity report about Madoff in the U.S., and forfeited $1.7 billion. In October 2008 the bank's London branch had reported to UK authorities that Madoff's returns appeared 'too good to be true'.

facts.claim: In 2023, JPMorgan Chase agreed to pay $290 million to settle a lawsuit brought on behalf of Jeffrey Epstein's victims and $75 million to settle a suit by the U.S. Virgin Islands alleging that the bank enabled and benefited from Epstein's sex trafficking. The bank did not admit liability.

JPMorgan to pay $75 million to settle lawsuit over ties with Jeffrey Epstein

facts.claim: The September 26, 2023 settlement with the U.S. Virgin Islands was for $75 million, less than half the $190 million the territory sought: $30 million for trafficking charities and a survivors' mental-health fund, $25 million for local infrastructure and law enforcement, and $20 million in attorneys' fees. The bank did not admit liability; the case had been set for trial in October 2023 before Judge Jed Rakoff.
facts.quote: The bank did not admit liability in agreeing to settle.

facts.claim: In its July 24, 2023 motion for partial summary judgment, the U.S. Virgin Islands alleged that by Epstein's 2006 arrest JPMorgan's compliance staff had been aware of alleged human trafficking and had noted he was 'known to pay cash for his massages' and that 'minors are the issue', and that the bank facilitated payments for more than 20,000 unlawful sex acts. These were the territory's allegations; the case settled before a ruling.
facts.quote: By the time of Epstein's 2006 arrest for prostitution in Palm Beach, Florida, the company's compliance staff had been aware of alleged human trafficking and acknowledged Epstein was "known to pay cash for his massages" and "minors are the issue," the U.S. Virgin Islands alleges in its motion for summary judgment.

sources.title: US Virgin Islands seeks judgment against JPMorgan for financing Epstein's sex trafficking

facts.claim: In March 2023 JPMorgan filed a third-party complaint against its former private-banking chief Jes Staley, alleging he helped conceal Epstein's conduct to keep him as a client; the bank and Staley settled on confidential terms in September 2023. Staley has expressed regret for the friendship and denied knowing of the trafficking.
facts.quote: JPMorgan Chase sued Staley in March, saying in a third-party complaint that he aided in hiding Epstein's yearslong sex abuse and trafficking to keep the financier as a client.

facts.claim: In late October 2025 Judge Rakoff, acting on requests by the New York Times and Wall Street Journal, ordered the unsealing of more than 100 summary-judgment exhibits from the Virgin Islands' suit; both sides agreed to release most documents except those identifying victims or containing Bank Secrecy Act-protected information.
facts.quote: U.S. District Judge Jed Rakoff broadly granted a request from The New York Times and The Wall Street Journal to release sealed exhibits from the summary judgment phase of the case.

sources.title: Federal Judge Unseals Scores of Documents From JPMorgan Civil Suit
Judge to unseal more than 100 documents in Epstein-related civil suit against JPMorgan Chase

facts.claim: A November 20, 2025 analysis by Senate Finance Committee ranking member Ron Wyden's staff, based on the unsealed records, states that JPMorgan processed more than $1 billion for Epstein over 15 years and reported only $4.3 million of transactions from his accounts in a handful of suspicious activity reports between 2002 and 2016; the memo calls for an investigation into whether the underreporting was deliberate. JPMorgan has not been found to have acted deliberately.

openQuestions: Epstein items appended 2026-10-09: no Rakoff opinion on the bank's internal flags was retrieved; the compliance-staff language is the USVI's allegation in its summary-judgment motion.
